title: Staff jobs phased out; recordings in public
summary: Automation, jukeboxes and TV replaced live musicians.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: How the music business changed: hype, youth and lost apprenticeship

blocks.x: Sure. That example you mentioned, when you first started in the studios on a weekly salary, with the promise that it was a lifetime job. That really wasn't a lifetime job, but now we don't have any staff at all.

No, they've completely phased us out, you know. Automation took over. You know, the jukeboxes, the TV sets in the bars. And I guess the bars had to have the TV sets because if they didn't, people would stay home and not come to the bars.

I think, though, that the downfall of everything started with recordings. In the '20s and '30s, people like Fred Waring and a lot of other people fought commercial use of recordings, public use of recordings. And when the union conceded that, or didn't do enough -- and again, I put everything on the union and the union means the membership, too. You know what a divided membership we've got. If we'd ever had any solid kind of action and got something done in Congress about it -- there was something done. It says on the records, 'Not for commercial use.' Which meant nothing. They played them on all the radio shows, every small station.
That's true. They played those things on all the stations. But now they don't even have that little circle on the record that says, this is for home consumption only. When did that disappear?

I don't know. It never meant anything anyhow. And, you know, if entertainment in public was not permitted, well, again, I don't know. You talk about free enterprise and the American system and everything. You don't really know how much should be done. As a musician, I wish that they didn't allow bars and places like that to have TV sets in them to use for entertainment, or jukeboxes. But, you know -- or Muzak. But, you and I know, it's ridiculous. It's not going away overnight. It's way past the time to do anything about it.
